title: The Verdier trace class is unconditionally defined
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions, $A=A_{E,n}$, put $s=\Spec k$, let
$c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times_sX$ be an
admissible cohomological
correspondence with fixed scheme
$F=\operatorname{Fix}(c)$, and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$. Then the
Verdier trace class
$\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)$ of [def-trf-trace-class] is defined for
every correspondence $u:Lc_2^*K\to Rc_1^!K$, under no hypothesis
beyond the admissibility of $c$ and $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$.

proof.text: Unpack [def-trf-correspondence]: $X$ and $C$ are separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Put $Z=X\times_sX$. A finite affine cover of $X$ gives a finite affine cover of $Z$ by rings $B\otimes_k B'$, which are finitely generated over $k$ using the generators of $B$ and $B'$. In $Z\times_sZ$, with coordinates $(x_1,x_2,y_1,y_2)$, the two equalities $x_1=y_1$ and $x_2=y_2$ define the pullbacks of the closed diagonal of $X$ along the two indicated projections. They are closed immersions by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]; their scheme-theoretic intersection is closed (on each affine open its ideal is the sum of the two ideals), and is exactly the diagonal of $Z$. Thus $Z$ is also separated of finite type. By [def-weil-proper-morphism], $\Delta_X:X\to Z$ is a closed immersion. The fibre-product definition [def-trf-fixed-scheme] and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] make $i_F:F\to C$ a closed immersion. On an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $C$ this is a quotient $B\twoheadrightarrow B/I$, a finite $B$-module generated by $1$, so $i_F$ is finite. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-separated-finite-type] to $F\to C\to s$: $F$ is separated of finite type over $k$.

source.place: last sentence: admissibility of the correspondence and its fixed scheme

proof.text: Every $k$-morphism $h:T\to Y$ among the separated finite-type schemes $F,C,X,Z,s$ is of finite type by [lemma-nagata-finite-type-to-separated-target], applied to $T\to Y\to s$. It is separated: its relative diagonal $T\to T\times_YT$ is the pullback of the closed diagonal $T\to T\times_sT$, hence is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. In particular this applies to $c,c_1,c_2,p_1,p_2,\Delta_X,i_F,d$ and the structure morphisms. Here $d=c_1i_F=c_2i_F$, as in the fixed-scheme definition used in Step 1.

source.place: last sentence: all morphisms used in the trace construction

proof.text: Apply the finite-stage clauses (1), (2), (4), and (8) of [sk-thm-sf-package] to these maps. They give the constructible adjunction $Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$, preservation of $D^b_{ctf}$, and the composition and exchange comparisons on the finite coefficient domain. These are precisely the constructible exceptional admissibility data specified in [def-trf-admissibility]. Thus the extra maps needed by the trace-map lemma are exceptionally admissible, and the structure maps define $\omega_{X,A}$ and $\omega_{F,A}$ as in [def-trf-dualizing-complex]. This uses the constructible adjoints, without an unrestricted ambient right-adjoint hypothesis. For each $n\geq1$ these are the finite-stage functors at $A=A_{E,n}$; the explicit bounds in clause (8) depend on the schemes and input amplitudes, not on $n$, so they also give the stage-independent constants in [def-trf-admissibility]. In particular, pullback, exceptional inverse image and internal Hom place $\mathcal H_c(K)$ in $D^b_{ctf}(C,A)$, and ordinary direct image places $Ra_{C*}\mathcal H_c(K)$ in $D^b_c(s,A)$.

source.place: second arrow and last sentence: exceptional admissibility required for the dualizing and trace maps

proof.text: For any given $u:Lc_2^*K\to Rc_1^!K$, the displayed tensor–internal-Hom bijection in [def-trf-trace-class-source] gives its mate $\widetilde u:A_C\to\mathcal H_c(K)$, with $\mathcal H_c(K)=R\mathcal Hom_A(Lc_2^*K,Rc_1^!K)$. Apply the ordinary pullback/direct-image adjunction, clause (1) of [sk-thm-sf-package], to $a_C:C\to s$ and use $La_C^*A_s=A_C$. Its image is a morphism $A_s\to Ra_{C*}\mathcal H_c(K)$. Apply the functor $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]: it sends $A_s$ to the coefficient complex $A$ and the target to $R\Gamma(C,\mathcal H_c(K))=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{C*}\mathcal H_c(K))$. This gives the required first arrow in the coefficient category. No invertibility of $u$ is required.

source.place: first arrow: the tensor–internal-Hom mate of an arbitrary correspondence

proof.text: The fixed scheme and its maps are those of Step 1, the coefficient complex is the given $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, and the exceptional admissibility of every map used has been checked in Steps 2–3. Therefore the statement of [lem-trf-trace-map-from-external-duality] applies and supplies the morphism $\mathfrak t_{c,K}:R\Gamma(C,\mathcal H_c(K))\to R\Gamma(F,\omega_{F,A})$. We use the trace-map lemma's stated existence assertion, without importing any additional property from its proof.

source.place: second arrow: the morphism supplied by lem-trf-trace-map-from-external-duality

proof.text: Compose the arrow obtained in Step 4 with the arrow in Step 5. The codomain of the first is exactly the domain of the second, so this gives $A\to R\Gamma(F,\omega_{F,A})$. By [def-trf-trace-class], this composite, viewed by global-sections adjunction as a morphism $A_F\to\omega_{F,A}$, is $\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)$. The adjunction identifies the set of such morphisms, not the object $R\Gamma(F,\omega_{F,A})$ with a Hom set. Every input has been obtained under the given hypotheses; consequently this trace class is defined for each $u$.

source.place: displayed composite and global-sections adjunction identification

proof_origin.place: entire proof; expanded admissibility and explicit composition of its two arrows

split_report.summary: Checked the current blueprint and Varshavsky 1.2.2(a), the trace-map lemma and every cited statement. Expanded the omitted admissibility check for the fixed-square maps using separated finite-type geometry and the finite-stage constructible six-functor package. Split the mate, trace-map application, and composite into distinct steps, and corrected the proof-only object/Hom-set wording. Statement unchanged; no new nodes. Second reader made the product diagonal and coefficient-level uniformity explicit and applied the geometric-point fibre functor in the first arrow.
split_report.blueprint: Steps 1–3 realize the last sentence of the blueprint proof by discharging the exceptional-admissibility hypotheses. Step 4 realizes its first arrow, Step 5 its second arrow, and Step 6 its displayed composite and global-sections adjunction. External duality and supported-pairing constructions remain inside the existing trace-map lemma rather than being recited as extra assumptions.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NS-ebb297617 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the full delivery and wrote no fixes. It changes only the report and the item, adds no new nodes, and keeps the statement verbatim from both the master and main-20261015 blueprints. proof_deps equals the union of the step uses. All 13 cited ids exist and are unmerged. A transitive dependency traversal does not reach the item, and def-trf-trace-class mentions it only as a forward pointer. No SGA source is used. Step 1 checks out: the diagonal of Z is the intersection of two pulled-back diagonals; i_F is the base change of Delta_X, so it is a closed immersion and hence finite; lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-separated-finite-type then makes F separated of finite type. Step 2 checks out: lemma-nagata-finite-type-to-separated-target applies with B=Spec k. Relative separatedness holds because T x_Y T -> T x_s T is a base change of Delta_Y, hence a monomorphism, so Delta_{T/Y} is the pullback of the closed diagonal Delta_T. I accept the declared tool use of lemma-nagata. One caveat: its blueprint_update would weaken it to 'locally of finite type', and Step 2 would then need one more line for quasi-compactness. Step 3 checks out against sk-thm-sf-package clauses (1), (2), (4) and (8): constructible Rf_! -| Rf^! on Dctf at A_{E,n} without the ambient FullCD datum, composition, Ex_!, and amplitude bounds independent of n. Those clauses supply exactly what def-trf-admissibility asks for and place H_c(K) and Ra_{C*}H_c(K) in the right categories. Step 4 checks out: the mate bijection of def-trf-trace-class-source needs no hypothesis on u; then La_C^* -| Ra_{C*} and Fib_s from def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology give A -> RGamma(C,H_c(K)), with the leg order matching def-trf-correspondence. Step 5 checks out: I read the proof of lem-trf-trace-map-from-external-duality, which needs admissibility of c, Delta_X, i_F and d, and Steps 2-3 cover all four. Varshavsky 1.2.2(a) (p.9 of the local PDF) builds the same trace map with no properness assumption. Step 6 checks out: it composes the two arrows as def-trf-trace-class states and correctly says the adjunction identifies Hom sets, not objects. Small cases all work: K=0, u=0, empty C, a correspondence with empty F, X=C=s with identity legs, and nonproper or nonreduced F. Details are in review.md.
